props.title: The Point
props.initialSlug: Boy born with round head faces pointy world

sections.content: The Point stands as a uniquely psychedelic animated fable that perfectly captures the free-thinking spirit of early 70s counterculture. Featuring Harry Nilsson's infectious songs and narration by Dustin Hoffman (later versions used Ringo Starr), it tells the story of Oblio, the only round-headed person in a world where everyone has points. Like Yellow Submarine (1968) and Fantastic Planet (1973), it uses bold animation to challenge conformity and celebrate individuality. The film's surreal visual style influenced later philosophical animations like The Wall (1982) and It's Such a Beautiful Day (2012).

sections.content: The film's animation style, created by Fred Wolf, uses minimalist line drawings and trippy color transitions that echo the experimental animation boom of the late 60s and early 70s. This era saw groundbreaking works like Fritz the Cat (1972) and Ralph Bakshi's Wizards (1977) push animation beyond children's entertainment. The Point maintains its kid-friendly narrative while embedding deeper messages about acceptance and questioning arbitrary social rules.

Nilsson's soundtrack album "The Point!" became a hit independent of the film, with songs like "Me and My Arrow" entering the pop culture zeitgeist. This success paved the way for other musician-driven animated projects like Pink Floyd: The Wall (1982) and Pete Townshend's The Iron Man (1989). The film's format - using animation to explore philosophical concepts through a child protagonist - influenced later works like The Little Prince (2015). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: The Point helped establish animation as a medium for countercultural messaging, joining contemporaries like Watership Down (1978) and Heavy Metal (1981) in proving animation could tackle serious themes. Its impact can be seen in modern independent animation like Persepolis (2007) and Mary and Max (2009), which similarly use simple yet striking visual styles to explore complex social issues.
